'''Sriram Rajagopal Ramaswamy''' (born 10 November 1957) is an Indian physicist. He is a professor at the [[Indian Institute of Science]], [[Bangalore]], and previously the director of the [[Tata Institute of Fundamental Research|Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR)]] Centre for Interdisciplinary Sciences in [[Hyderabad]].<ref name=googlescholar>{{GoogleScholar|igytGcAAAAAJ}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304002157/http://www.physics.iisc.ernet.in/~sriram/|archive-date=2016-03-04|url=http://www.physics.iisc.ernet.in/~sriram/|title=Sriram Ramaswamy Homepage|publisher=iisc.ernet.in}}</ref><ref name=cv>{{cite web|archive-date=2016-05-12|url=http://www.tifrh.res.in/tcis/faculty/srcv.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160512211423/http://www.tifrh.res.in/tcis/faculty/srcv.pdf|title=Sriram Ramaswamy CV|publisher=tifrh.res.in|location=Hyderabad}}</ref>

==Education==
Ramaswamy completed high school at the [[Modern School (New Delhi)|Modern School, Barakhamba Road, New Delhi]], and then moved to the [[University of Maryland]] where he was awarded a Bachelor of Science degree in [[Physics]] with high honours in 1977.<ref name=cv/> He completed his PhD in [[theoretical physics]] at the [[University of Chicago]], graduating in 1983.<ref name=phd>{{cite thesis |degree=PhD |first=Sriram Rajagopal|last=Ramaswamy |title=Solid like behavior in liquid layers: a theory of the yield stress in smectics |publisher=University of Chicago |year=1983 |url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/303282658/ |oclc=17122087}}</ref> He completed [[postdoctoral research]] at the [[University of Pennsylvania]].<ref name=infosys/>

==Research==
Ramaswamy is a theoretician whose research investigates nonequilibrium statistical physics, [[soft matter]], [[condensed matter physics]] and [[biophysics|biological physics]].<ref name=googlescholar/> His research helped found the field of [[active matter]], which studies the [[motility]] and related collective behaviour of objects that convert local energy input into autonomous motion.<ref name=frs/>

He is widely known for formulating the [[hydrodynamic]] equations<ref name=MarchettiJoanny2013>{{cite journal|last1=Marchetti|first1=M. C.|last2=Joanny|first2=J. F.|last3=Ramaswamy|first3=S.|last4=Liverpool|first4=T. B.|last5=Prost|first5=J.|last6=Rao|first6=Madan|last7=Simha|first7=R. Aditi|title=Hydrodynamics of soft active matter|journal=Reviews of Modern Physics|volume=85|issue=3|year=2013|pages=1143–1189|doi=10.1103/RevModPhys.85.1143|bibcode=2013RvMP...85.1143M}}</ref><ref name=TonerTu2005>{{cite journal|last1=Toner|first1=John|last2=Tu|first2=Yuhai|last3=Ramaswamy|first3=Sriram|title=Hydrodynamics and phases of flocks|journal=Annals of Physics|volume=318|issue=1|year=2005|pages=170–244|doi=10.1016/j.aop.2005.04.011|bibcode=2005AnPhy.318..170T|url=http://eprints.iisc.ac.in/3397/1/A89.pdf}}</ref> governing the alignment, flow, mechanics and statistical properties of suspensions of self-propelled creatures, on scales from a cell to the ocean.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Kumar|first1=Abhishek|last2=Maitra|first2=Ananyo|last3=Sumit|first3=Madhuresh|last4=Ramaswamy|first4=Sriram|last5=Shivashankar|first5=G. V.|date=2014-01-21|title=Actomyosin contractility rotates the cell nucleus|journal=Scientific Reports|language=En|volume=4|issue=1|page=3781|doi=10.1038/srep03781|doi-access=free|pmid=24445418|pmc=3896915|issn=2045-2322|bibcode=2014NatSR...4.3781K}}</ref><ref name=Ramaswamy2010>{{cite journal|last1=Ramaswamy|first1=Sriram|title=The Mechanics and Statistics of Active Matter|journal=Annual Review of Condensed Matter Physics|volume=1|issue=1|year=2010|pages=323–345|arxiv=1004.1933|doi=10.1146/annurev-conmatphys-070909-104101|bibcode=2010ARCMP...1..323R|s2cid=55500360 }}</ref> Key predictions—that macroscopically aligned [[Flocking (behavior)|flocks]] of swimming bacteria are impossible, and that the addition of swimmers to a fluid can make the [[viscosity]] arbitrarily small—have been confirmed in recent experiments. His insight into nonliving imitations of self-propulsion has led to design principles for [[chemotactic]] [[colloid]]s, the first experiments observing giant number fluctuations in flocks, and the creation of flocks with a tiny minority of motile constituents.<ref name=frs/><ref name=NarayanRamaswamy2007>{{cite journal|last1=Narayan|first1=V.|last2=Ramaswamy|first2=S.|last3=Menon|first3=N.|title=Long-Lived Giant Number Fluctuations in a Swarming Granular Nematic|journal=Science|volume=317|issue=5834|year=2007|pages=105–108|arxiv=cond-mat/0612020|doi=10.1126/science.1140414|pmid=17615353|bibcode=2007Sci...317..105N|s2cid=3178657 }}</ref><ref name=LevineLubensky1985>{{cite journal|last1=Levine|first1=Dov|last2=Lubensky|first2=T. C.|last3=Ostlund|first3=Stellan|last4=Ramaswamy|first4=Sriram|last5=Steinhardt|first5=Paul Joseph|last6=Toner|first6=John|title=Elasticity and Dislocations in Pentagonal and Icosahedral Quasicrystals|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=54|issue=14|year=1985|pages=1520–1523|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.54.1520|pmid=10031060|bibcode=1985PhRvL..54.1520L}}</ref><ref name=AditiSimhaRamaswamy2002>{{cite journal|last1=Aditi Simha|first1=R.|last2=Ramaswamy|first2=Sriram|title=Hydrodynamic Fluctuations and Instabilities in Ordered Suspensions of Self-Propelled Particles|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=89|issue=5|year=2002|arxiv=cond-mat/0108301|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.89.058101|pmid=12144468|article-number=058101|bibcode=2002PhRvL..89e8101A|s2cid=3845736 }}</ref><ref name=KumarSoni2014>{{cite journal|last1=Kumar|first1=Nitin|last2=Soni|first2=Harsh|last3=Ramaswamy|first3=Sriram|last4=Sood|first4=A. K.|author-link4=Ajay K. Sood|title=Flocking at a distance in active granular matter|journal=Nature Communications|volume=5|year=2014|page=4688|arxiv=1402.4262|doi=10.1038/ncomms5688|doi-access=free|pmid=25181961|bibcode=2014NatCo...5.4688K|s2cid=19244108 }}</ref>

==Awards and honours==
Among the awards he has received for his research are the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology]] in 2000 and the [[Infosys Prize]] for Physical Sciences in 2011.<ref name=infosys>{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160322101432/http://www.infosys-science-foundation.com/prize/laureates/2011/sriram-ramaswamy.asp|archive-date=2016-03-22|url=http://www.infosys-science-foundation.com/prize/laureates/2011/sriram-ramaswamy.asp|publisher=infosys-science-foundation.com|title=Professor Sriram Ramaswamy: Physical Sciences, 2011}}</ref> He also served on the Physical Sciences jury for the [[Infosys Prize]] in 2014. He was elected a [[List of Fellows of the Royal Society elected in 2016|Fellow of the Royal Society (FRS) in 2016]].<ref name=frs>{{cite web |url=https://royalsociety.org/people/sriram-ramaswamy-12893/ |title=Professor Sriram Ramaswamy FRS |publisher=[[Royal Society]] |archive-date=2016-04-29 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160429121447/https://royalsociety.org/people/sriram-ramaswamy-12893/ |location=London |author=Anon |year=2016 }} One or more of the preceding sentences incorporates text from the royalsociety.org website where: {{blockquote|"All text published under the heading 'Biography' on Fellow profile pages is available under [[Creative Commons license|Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License]]." --{{cite web |url=https://royalsociety.org/about-us/terms-conditions-policies/ |title=Royal Society Terms, conditions and policies |access-date=2016-03-09 |url-status=bot: unknown |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150925220834/https://royalsociety.org/about-us/terms-conditions-policies/ |archive-date=25 September 2015 }}}}</ref>

He was awarded one of the [[H K Firodia awards]] for 2016.<ref>{{cite web|url= http://hkfirodiaawards.org/awards_2.html|title= Celebrating 22 Years of H. K. Firodia Awards for Excellence in Science & Technology|publisher= H. K. Firodia Memorial Foundation|access-date= 1 May 2018|archive-date= 4 March 2016|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20160304234211/http://hkfirodiaawards.org/awards_2.html}}</ref> He was elected an International Member of the US National Academy of Sciences in 2025.<ref>{{Cite web | title=National Academy of Sciences Elects Members and International Members - NAS | url=https://www.nasonline.org/news/2025-nas-election/ | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250429230413/https://www.nasonline.org/news/2025-nas-election/ | access-date=2026-09-05 | archive-date=2025-04-29}}</ref>
